final_message:
I've built the Excel workbook. It recommends **USPS for Pak and Small Box, and UPS for Medium, Large and Extra Large Box**. FedEx is not the cheapest option for any size. Projected 2026 flat-rate cost for that split is **$93,476**, which is $18,372 (16%) less than using the next-cheapest carrier for every size.

| Size (2026 units) | Use | Projected 2026 cost | Saving vs next best |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pak (1,000) | USPS Padded Flat Rate Envelope, commercial price | $11,050 | $3,490 vs FedEx |
| Small Box (2,300) | USPS Small Flat Rate Box, commercial price | $25,668 | $10,557 vs UPS |
| Medium Box (2,100) | UPS Simple Rate Ground, business rates | $39,627 | $1,260 vs USPS (3%) |
| Large Box (540) | UPS Simple Rate Ground, business rates | $13,419 | $1,987 vs USPS |
| Extra Large Box (120) | UPS Simple Rate Ground, business rates | $3,712 | $1,078 vs FedEx |

- **Estimated 2026 increase:** I applied each carrier's own 2020–2025 average. That is 5.73% for UPS and FedEx (both raised list rates by the same amount every year). For USPS it is 5.27%, based on Priority Mail, the service that includes its flat-rate boxes. USPS raised prices twice in 2025, and I combined the two into one 9.7% increase for that year.
- **Exclusions:** USPS has no Extra Large flat-rate box, so it is left out for that size. UPS's flat-rate program has no Pak size, so it is left out for Pak. I treated the USPS Padded Flat Rate Envelope as its Pak.
- **Delivery speed:** USPS Priority Mail and UPS Ground are the standard services. FedEx's flat-rate program only covers its faster air services, so I used the slowest one, Express Saver (3 business days).
- **Base prices and timing:** It is now November 2026, so 2026 prices are already published. Raising them by an estimated 2026 increase would count the increase twice. Instead, the projection starts from the last prices published before 2026 and adds the estimate.
- **Check against actual 2026 prices:** the recommendation holds for every size. That includes USPS's temporary 8% increase from April 26, 2026 and its holiday surcharge from October 4, 2026.
- **FedEx under-estimate:** FedEx's flat rates actually rose 12.5–18.6%, well above its 5.9% average, so the projection understates FedEx's cost. That only makes FedEx look worse.

**Decision for you:** Medium Box is the close call, at about 3% in UPS's favour. UPS charges by the size of your own box, so its Medium rate applies only to boxes of 251–650 cubic inches. If our standard medium box measures bigger, UPS bills it as Large and the USPS Medium box becomes cheaper. Someone needs to measure our box before the team acts on this.

**Gaps:**
- **No company files:** the reference, workspace and attachments folders were empty, so there was no internal operations record or registry to use.
- **UPS 2026 prices:** UPS's site blocked direct download of its 2026 rate guide. I took those prices from the search engine's copy of the official file, and a second website shows the same figures.
- **FedEx early-2026 prices:** I couldn't find FedEx's flat-rate prices for January 5 to April 19, 2026, so I left them out rather than estimate them.

The workbook also has the shipping team's exception rules (Alaska/Hawaii, items that don't fit, over 50 lb, extra services like signature or insurance), the assumptions, and a sources sheet with every URL and its retrieval date (2026-11-05). I checked every formula with a separate Python calculator and the results match. The file was built without Excel, so the numbers only appear once it's opened in Excel, which calculates them on open.

DONE

Files are in `outputs/`:
